newsitem.title: UK: Consumer coffee stocks fall in September - ED&F Man.
newsitem.headline: Consumer coffee stocks fall in September - ED&F Man.

text.p: World consumer coffee stocks stood at 8.7 million bags in September, down from 9.0 million in August and 1.80 million lower than in September last year, British trade house E D & F Man said.
The supply situation was very tight in the United States where stocks totalled only 1.61 million bags, down by 205,000 bags from a month earlier and 997,000 a year ago.
"This (1.61 million bags) is the lowest since statistics have been collected and U.S. mild coffee stocks must now be near minimum working levels," it said.

European stocks fell 100,000 bags to 5.90 million bags in September from a month ago.Japanese stocks were 1.09 million, up slightly from 1.06 million in August but down by 262,000 bags from September 1995.
Man said European roasters were still better covered than their counterparts in the U.S. having taken more physical coverage of Central American coffee during the peak shipment period.
"Some European roasters even believe that stocks in Europe could be reduced by a further week of regional demand, equivalent to around 750,000 bags of coffee," it said.
Man said European warehouses were meanwhile reporting an increase in robusta arrivals during October.
"Uganda and Ivory Coast arrivals are said to be picking up and the first shipments from the Vietnam new crop are said to be unloading in the European robusta ports," it said.
